A helper for writing and understanding text, with no internet. A small language model (Qwen3 0.6B) runs fully on this phone.
Rewriting, shortening, explaining, summarising and drafting text you give it.
Facts, news, dates, numbers, maths, and medical or legal answers. It can sound sure and still be wrong.
Arivu has no permission to use the internet. Your messages stay only on this phone and are not backed up.
If Arivu wrote something offensive or harmful, tap Report under that reply. You can also send a general report here. Both open your email or messaging app. Nothing is sent until you send it.

Privacy policy for Arivu on Android, version %1$s.

Arivu has no permission to use the internet. Android does not let it send anything anywhere.

What you type and what Arivu writes is stored only on your phone, in the app’s private storage. It is not included in phone backups or phone-to-phone transfers.

We do not collect, receive, sell or share your messages. There is no account, no advertising, no analytics and no crash-reporting software in the app.

If you choose to report a reply, Arivu prepares an email with that reply and your note. You check it, and your own email app sends it. We receive only what you send.
Arivu cannot connect to the internet

Arivu does not ask Android for the internet permission or for permission to see your network. It asks only for permissions that show no pop-up and give no access to the internet or your personal data: to keep writing a reply for a short time if you switch apps, to open Android’s uninstall screen for Arivu itself on a phone that cannot run it, and one that Google’s AndroidX library adds so other apps cannot send Arivu internal messages.
What is stored on your phone

Your conversation: the messages you send, the replies, when each was created, why a reply stopped, and whether you reported it. It is one file in Arivu’s private storage, kept until you uninstall Arivu or clear its storage. If that file is ever damaged, Arivu keeps only the newest damaged copy there and starts a new conversation.

A note that your phone passed Arivu’s compatibility check, so the check does not run on every launch.

Backup and phone-to-phone transfer are turned off for all of Arivu’s storage. The file is not encrypted by Arivu itself; it is protected by Android’s app sandbox and your phone’s own encryption and screen lock. Anyone who can unlock your phone and open Arivu can read the conversation.

Nothing, through the app. Arivu contains no analytics, advertising, tracking, crash-reporting or payment software, and it cannot send data. We never see your messages, and they are not used to train any AI model.

Under each reply there is a Report button, and there is a general Report button on this screen. Report opens your own email app (or, if you have none, Android’s share menu) with our address, a subject and the app version. A report from under a reply also adds the reason you chose, your note and the text of that reply — only that reply, not the rest of the conversation. The general report on this screen is a blank form. Nothing is sent until you press send, and that app, not Arivu, sends it. Arivu marks the reply as reported on your phone.\n\nIf you send a report, we receive what is in it and whatever your email service adds, such as your email address. We use reports only to understand harmful replies, make Arivu safer and reply to you if needed. We do not sell or share them, and we delete them when we no longer need them. You can ask us to delete your report sooner.

Copy puts text on your phone’s clipboard, like any copied text. Arivu asks your keyboard app not to learn from what you type here, but Arivu cannot see or control what your keyboard app does. Other apps work under their own privacy policies.

You install and update Arivu through Google Play, which has its own privacy policy. Google gives developers summary statistics, such as installs by country and device model, and crash statistics from people who chose to share them with Google. Installing uses data. Once installed, Arivu itself uses none.
Arivu is not designed for children. The app collects nothing from anyone. If a child has sent us a report, write to us and we will delete it.

To delete your conversation, uninstall Arivu, or open Android Settings, then Apps, Arivu, Storage, Clear storage. Arivu is open source, so anyone can check these claims. Depending on where you live, you may have further rights over a report you sent us, and you can complain to your data protection authority.
If a future version changes what Arivu stores or sends, this policy changes before that version is released. A version that needed the internet would be a different app, and we would say so plainly.
Arivu can’t run well on this phone
Arivu runs a language model on the phone itself. That needs more than this phone has. Rather than run slowly or crash, Arivu will not start.
This phone’s processor is not a 64-bit ARM processor (arm64-v8a).
This phone is set up as a low-memory device.
